newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks salvage minor gain in huge session.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks salvage minor gain in huge session.

text.p: Taiwan's share index blistered to within 115 points of 10,000 and a seven-year intraday high on Thursday, but lost momentum in the final minutes to salvage only a modest closing gain on all-time record turnover.
The electronics sector, which led the early charge on steam from Wall Street's high-tech rally, nosedived in late trade as investors took profits and shifted to other major sectors.
The benchmark index throttled technical resistance at 9,600 to notch a sizzling seven-year intraday high 9,889.45, but ended with a gain of just 27.24 points or 0.29 percent at 9,571.8.
Turnover screamed to a historic high T$296.8 billion.
The weighted index freefell some 300 points in last minutes, with electronics dumped heavily near the close, brokers said.
"It was just dramatic, especially in the electronic sector, which had risen more than six percent in early trade, but ended three percent lower," Lei Pei-yu of Pacific Securities said.
The electronics sector lost 3.5 percent, with early seven percent limit-up gains of many firms erased, brokers said.

A significant exception was motherboard giant Asustek, which managed to hold on to its T$34 limit-up gain to end at T$529. Computer maker Systex, which soared in early trade, swallowed a T$6 loss to end at T$81.
Despite electronics' fall, other major sectors, including plastics, textiles and constructions, had technical rebounds to post impressive gains, brokers said.
Plastics chalked up 6.33 percent surge, with Taiwan Polypropelene rising T$2.5 to T$38.3.
Textiles bounded 3.43 percent higher, with Hong Yi Fiber climbing up T$2 to T$31.

Brokers said margin-buying credit limits that kicked in when the index hit 9,600 weres no longer a concern as investors were active in buying electronic shares in early trade and later used their gains to buy other shares, rather than cashing out.
